observation: Across five gfx1151 tasks, two task-dependent sample positions separated by sixteen repeatedly exceed their cohort-arm median by more than 20%. The retained diagnostic counts candidate outliers at positions 6/22 in 276/261 of 320 momentum_sgd cohorts, 4/20 in 145/143 of 210 adamw cohorts, 8/24 in 302/307 of 320 softmax_backward cohorts, 8/24 in 243/251 of 260 absmax_rescale cohorts, and 7/23 in 278/283 of 310 rmsnorm_input_gradient cohorts (zero-based positions). The median absolute excess at those positions is about 4.5-5.0 microseconds. The same absolute excess has a larger relative effect on a shorter candidate than on its slower fixed baseline. The pattern is repeatable, but these records do not distinguish profiler buffering, reset scheduling, or device interference as its cause. It is not evidence that the candidate kernel itself slowed periodically.
proposed_change: First run a no-change A/A timing probe on an idle gfx1151 under the admitted runtime, retaining raw per-dispatch events. Vary only profiler session chunk size while keeping the exact kernel, inputs, device-state reset and sample count fixed, then compare the position and magnitude of spikes. If the timing source is responsible, introduce a reviewed successor timing protocol and calibrated timer implementation with tests and new device evidence; keep all frozen Run outcomes and their original CV gate unchanged. Do not trim periodic samples, loosen maximum_cv, or reclassify quality-failed candidates from this diagnostic alone.
